en: Hey, Slovaks, our Slovak speech still lives,
As long as our faithful heart beats for our nation.
It lives, it lives, the Slovak spirit, it will live for ever,
Thunder and hell, your rages against us are in vain!
God entrusted to us the gift of language, God our ruler of thunder,
So no one in this world may tear it from us;
And let there be as many devils in the world as there are people;
God is with us: whoever is against us, Parom will sweep him away.
And even if a terrible storm should rise above us,
The rock splits, the oak breaks, and let the earth shake;
We stand ever firm, like the walls of a castle.
The black earth will swallow him who treacherously deserts!
notes: line 2.2: 'Hrom a peklo' (thunder and hell) is addressed to the song's enemies as an oath-like cry.
line 4.2: 'Parom' is the Slovak name of Perun, the old Slavic god of thunder; kept as a name.
line 6.2: 'kto odstúpi zradne' = whoever steps back (falls away) treacherously.
